title: Best Dehumidifier (2026): Top House Dehumidifiers Compared
dek: Musty basement, clammy bedroom or a crawl space you'd rather not think about — here's the right machine for each, and how to size it.
description: The best house dehumidifiers of 2026 for basements, bedrooms and crawl spaces, compared on DOE pint ratings, drainage, low-temp operation and running cost.
intro: Damp air rarely announces itself. It shows up as a musty smell when you open the basement door, a bloom of black spots on a bathroom ceiling, sheets that never feel quite dry. A good house dehumidifier is the fix: the EPA notes that mold can take hold on a damp surface within **24 to 48 hours**, and its single best piece of advice is to keep indoor relative humidity between **30% and 50%**.

A good dehumidifier does that for you, quietly and automatically. The catch is that the category is crowded with near-identical white boxes, confusing pint ratings and marketing claims that don't line up with federal test data. So we compared the leading models on the things that actually separate them: rated moisture removal under the current DOE test, how the water leaves the machine, whether it keeps working in a cold basement, and what it costs to run.
Below are our six picks, from a do-everything 50-pint unit to a tiny closet machine and a commercial-grade crawl space dehumidifier, plus a plain-English guide to choosing the right size.
topPicksLead: Our top pick is the **Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT)**, which pairs full 50-pint capacity with a reservoir so large you empty it every few days instead of twice a day.

products.name: Midea Cube 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD50S1QWT)
pros: Huge reservoir base means far less emptying
Owners and reviewers report unusually fast pull-down

products.whyWeLoveIt: The Cube fixes the most tedious part of owning a dehumidifier: the bucket. Its whole lower half is a water reservoir that holds about 4.35 gallons, so in a damp basement you can go days between trips. Add a sharp app and solid capacity, and it's the easiest dehumidifier to live with.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR lists it at 49.67 pints a day under the 2019 DOE test, which is full 50-pint-class capacity, and Midea rates it for up to 4,500 sq ft. Independent reviewers have repeatedly singled it out for how quickly it drags a soggy room down to the 40s. Its efficiency sits right at the ENERGY STAR line for its class, so expect running costs in line with other 50-pint units. Our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide covers the 20- and 35-pint siblings and the pump version.

blocks.text: That last figure trips up a lot of shoppers. The DOE now tests dehumidifiers at 65°F instead of 80°F, which is closer to real basement conditions but produces smaller numbers. A unit labeled 50 pints today removes roughly what an old 70-pint model claimed. Always compare pint ratings under the same test.

sections.heading: How we pick the best dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We're researchers, not a test lab. Our shortlist starts with data that's comparable across brands: capacity and efficiency under the 2019 DOE procedure from ENERGY STAR's certified-product list, plus manufacturer manuals and spec sheets for drainage, minimum operating temperature, humidistat range and warranty.

We check every pick against the CPSC recall database — dehumidifiers have a long recall history tied to overheating — and then read owner reviews in bulk to find recurring problems such as leaking buckets, failing pumps and sensors that drift. We also weigh results from reputable published third-party testing where it exists. Models that look great on paper but show a pattern of early failures don't make the cut.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier

items.label: The right capacity
items.text: Size by DOE pints and how damp the space is. A damp bedroom needs about 20 pints; a wet basement or large open floor, 35 to 50. When in doubt, size up — a bigger unit cycles less. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the full chart.

items.label: Drainage that fits the space
items.text: A bucket works for a room you walk through daily. For a basement or crawl space, use a gravity hose (needs a drain below the unit) or a built-in pump that pushes water up and out.

items.label: Cold-weather capability
items.text: Basements, garages and crawl spaces get chilly. Look for auto-defrost and a stated low-temperature range if the space dips below about 65°F; below 40°F, consider a desiccant model.

items.label: A real humidistat
items.text: A set-a-number control lets the unit cycle off once it reaches your target, saving energy and preventing over-drying.

items.label: Efficiency
items.text: Compressor units typically draw 300 to 700 watts while running. ENERGY STAR certification and a good humidistat keep bills reasonable — see our [best energy efficient dehumidifier](/best/best-energy-efficient-dehumidifier/) picks.

blocks.title: One flood, or everyday damp?
blocks.text: If you're drying out after a single leak or flood, renting a commercial unit can make more sense than buying one. Our [dehumidifier rental](/guides/dehumidifier-rental/) guide runs the numbers.

For most homes, the **Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT)** is the dehumidifier to buy: fast, capacious and easy to live with. Pick the **hOmeLabs HME1003** if your basement is large and wet and you want a pump, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** to save money, the **Frigidaire Gallery** for premium features, the **Pro Breeze PB-03** for a closet or small room, and the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65** for a crawl space. Whichever you choose, aim for 30–50% humidity and keep up with the simple filter and coil habits in our [dehumidifier maintenance](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) guide.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier in 2026?
faqs.a: For most homes, the Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT). It has full 50-pint-class capacity, an oversized 4.35-gallon reservoir and app control. For a wet basement with no low drain, the hOmeLabs HME1003 with a built-in pump is a better fit.

faqs.q: Should I get a portable or a whole-house dehumidifier?
faqs.a: A portable house dehumidifier dries the room or floor it sits in and plugs into an ordinary outlet. A ducted whole-house system ties into your HVAC and holds every room at one setpoint, but it costs far more and needs professional installation. If the damp is mostly in a basement, start with a portable; see our [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) picks if every floor feels clammy.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need?
faqs.a: Match the DOE pint rating to both size and dampness. Around 20 pints suits a damp bedroom; 35 to 50 pints suits a damp basement or large open area. If you're between sizes, go bigger — the unit will cycle less and hold its setpoint more easily.

faqs.q: Do I need a dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: Only if you want continuous drainage and there's no drain lower than the unit. A gravity hose works when a floor drain sits below the machine; a pump is needed to push water up to a sink or out a window, as in most below-grade basements.

faqs.q: What humidity should I set my dehumidifier to?
faqs.a: The EPA recommends 30% to 50% relative humidity indoors. Most people set 45% to 50% in summer. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has room-by-room targets.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to run a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: A typical 50-pint compressor unit draws about 300 to 700 watts while the compressor is on. How much you pay depends on your electricity rate, your setpoint and how damp the space is; a good humidistat that cycles the unit off makes the biggest difference.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier get rid of mold?
faqs.a: It won't remove existing mold, but holding humidity below 50% stops new growth. Clean visible mold first, then let the dehumidifier keep conditions dry. Our guide to [whether a dehumidifier helps with mold](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/) goes deeper.
